arxiv-2006-00957.title: Critical pressure asymmetry in the enclosed fluid diode
arxiv-2006-00957.creator: Jack R. Panter, Yonas Gizaw, Halim Kusumaatmaja
arxiv-2006-00957.description: Abstract Joint physically and chemically pattered surfaces can provide efficient and passive manipulation of fluid flow. The ability of many of these surfaces to allow only unidirectional flow mean they are often referred to as fluid diodes. Synthetic analogues of these are enabling technologies from sustainable water collection via fog harvesting, to improved wound dressings.

arxiv-2205-07801.title: Large rank jumps on elliptic surfaces and the Hilbert property
arxiv-2205-07801.creator: Renato Dias Costa, Cecília Salgado
arxiv-2205-07801.description: Abstract . Given a rational elliptic surface over a number field, we study the collection of fibers whose Mordell–Weil rank is greater than the generic rank. We give conditions on the singular fibers to assure that the collection of fibers for which the rank jumps of at least 3 is not thin.

arxiv-2208-07347.title: Charmenability and Stiffness of Arithmetic Groups
arxiv-2208-07347.creator: Uri Bader, Itamar Vigdorovich
arxiv-2208-07347.description: Abstract We characterize charmenability among arithmetic groups and deduce dichotomy statements pertaining normal subgroups, characters, dynamics, representations and associated operator algebras. We do this by studying the stationary dynamics on the space of characters of the amenable radical, and in particular we establish stiffness: any stationary probability measure is invariant.

arxiv-2308-07922.title: Raven : In-Context Learning with Retrieval-Augmented Encoder-Decoder Language Models
arxiv-2308-07922.creator: Jie Huang Wei Ping Peng Xu Mohammad Shoeybi, Kevin Chen-Chuan Chang Bryan Catanzaro
arxiv-2308-07922.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the in-context learning ability of retrieval-augmented encoder-decoder language models. We first conduct a comprehensive analysis of existing models and identify their limitations in in-context learning, primarily due to a mismatch between pretraining and inference, as well as a restricted context length.

arxiv-2506-03179.title: Vid-SME: Membership Inference Attacks against Large Video Understanding Models
arxiv-2506-03179.creator: Qi LiRunpeng Yu, Xinchao WangNational University of Singapore {liqi, r.yu}@u.nus.eduxinchao@nus.edu.sg
arxiv-2506-03179.description: Abstract Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) demonstrate remarkable capabilities in handling complex multimodal tasks and are increasingly adopted in video understanding applications. However, their rapid advancement raises serious data privacy concerns, particularly given the potential inclusion of sensitive video content, such as personal recordings and surveillance footage, in their training datasets.

arxiv-2510-23385.title: On the choking mechanism in supersonic ejectors: a one-dimensional analysis of Reynolds-Averaged Navier Stokes simulations
arxiv-2510-23385.creator: Jan Van den Berghe 1,2, Miguel A. Mendez 1,3,4, Yann Bartosiewicz 2
arxiv-2510-23385.description: Abstract Ejectors are passive devices used in refrigeration, propulsion, and process industries to compress a secondary stream without moving parts. The engineering modeling of choking in these devices remains an open question, with two mechanisms—Fabri and compound choking—proposed in the literature.

arxiv-2510-27176.title: Glia: A Human-Inspired AI for Automated Systems Design and Optimization
arxiv-2510-27176.creator: Pouya Hamadanian, Pantea Karimi, Arash Nasr-Esfahany, Kimia Noorbakhsh, [4pt] Joseph Chandler, Ali ParandehGheibi, Mohammad Alizadeh, Hari Balakrishnan, [12pt] Equal contribution (alphabetical order)
arxiv-2510-27176.description: Abstract Can an AI autonomously design mechanisms for computer systems on par with the creativity and reasoning of human experts? We present Glia, an AI architecture for networked systems design that uses large language models (LLMs) in a human-inspired, multi-agent workflow.

arxiv-2511-00332.title: On the spectral properties of long-range perturbations of a class of block finite difference operators
arxiv-2511-00332.creator: Olivier Bourget, Angela Vargas-Mancipe
arxiv-2511-00332.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Olivier Bourget, Angela Vargas-Mancipe. We analyze spectral properties of a family of self-adjoint first-order finite difference operators acting on ℓ 2 ​ ( ℤ , ℂ 2 ) \ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C}^{2}) or ℓ 2 ​ ( ℤ + , ℂ 2 ) \ell^{2}(\mathbb{Z}_{+};\mathbb{C}^{2}) . Applying the conjugate operator method, we prove the existence of limiting absorption principles and the absence of singular continuous spectrum for these operators. Our results cover classes of admissible long-range perturbations that have not been previously addressed.

arxiv-2601-10056.title: Anomalous transport in quasiperiodic lattices: emergent exceptional points at band edges and log-periodic oscillations
arxiv-2601-10056.creator: Jinyuan Shang, Haiping Hu
arxiv-2601-10056.description: Abstract Quasiperiodic systems host exotic transport regimes that are distinct from those found in periodic or disordered lattices. In this work, we study quantum transport in the Aubry-André-Harper lattice in a two-terminal setup coupled to zero-temperature reservoirs, where the conductance is evaluated via the nonequilibrium Green’s function method.

pmc-10710186.title: Identification of Key Genes for Pyroptosis-Induced Salivary Gland Inflammation in Sjogren’s Syndrome Based on Microarray Data and Immunohistochemistry Analysis
pmc-10710186.creator: Kaiyuan Zhang, Ziyue Luo, Xinchao Zhu, Xinyi Yao, Dingqi Lu, Liying Chen, Tao Hong, Yating Ren, Xinchang Wang
pmc-10710186.description: PurposeSjogren’s Syndrome (SS) is a systemic autoimmune disease primarily characterized by dysfunction of the exocrine glands. Research into the etiology and pathogenesis of salivary glands (SG) inflammation of SS is very limited. The aim of this study was to identify potential pyroptosis-related genes in SG inflammation through bioinformatics analysis and validation of the SG in SS.

pmc-11654092.title: ALK + anaplastic large cell lymphoma involving the bladder: case report and review of the literature
pmc-11654092.creator: Ying Zhao, Wenqiang Qiu, Xiangtao Weng, Chiming Gu, Siyi Li
pmc-11654092.description: We reported a case of anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALK + ALCL) involving the bladder. The patient was a 27-year-old female, whose main clinical symptoms included fever, painless lymphadenopathy, and hematuria. Imaging studies suggested a bladder mass. The bladder mass was maximally resected through transurethral bladder tumor resection.

pmc-12654491.description: The technology of 3D printing has become one of the most effective methods of creating various parts, such as those used for fast prototyping. The most important aspect of 3D printing is the selection and application of the appropriate material, also known as filament.

pmc-12987779.creator: Stephen P. Hibbs, Rumman Nizam, Ubaid Tanzim, Laura Aiken, Sabrina Habib, Sam Hodgson, Jill Williams, Adam Januszewski, Andrew Hantel, Mohammed Salah Uddin, Talia Isaacs, Bettina Bajaj, Olivia Cockburn, Amin Islam, Guy Pratt, Federico M. Federici
